summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 14, part 108) in which a teenager named Nikko is interviewed by FBI agents Martens and Jankovich about a college student, Simon Meyer, whom Nikko suspects of planning something. Nikko plays two recordings, the agents make small talk and probe him, and Martens tells him he is too young for dangerous work and must stay away from Meyer. Nikko protests that Meyer trusts him, but Martens dismisses him and says the agents will handle it.
one_line: In a fiction excerpt, FBI agents interview a seventeen-year-old who suspects college student Simon Meyer of plotting something, then send him away.
key_facts: Nikko is seventeen years old, a minor, according to the agents who checked his age.
Nikko played two recordings for the agents, who listened intently.
Nikko believes Simon Meyer is more than a typical college student who goes to demonstrations and talks a lot.
Agent Martens said the agents were taking the matter seriously and needed to find out whether Meyer was for real or just blowing smoke.
Nikko offered to introduce Meyer to one of the agents' undercover people.
Martens told Nikko that given his age, the agents could not ask him to take on a dangerous job.
Martens said it was against the rules for a minor to take on such work.
Martens instructed Nikko to stay away from Mr. Meyer and his big mouth, and to get out of any situation if Meyer tried to talk to him again.
Nikko argued that Meyer trusts him and that if they did not act now it could be too late.
Martens said the parents would be all over the agents if they put Nikko in such a situation.
Martens concluded with the line 'It ain't gonna happen' and said the agents had professionals in the field and 'We got this.'
Jankovich left the room for about five minutes to make a call and returned, and Martens said he wanted to recruit Nikko when he was older.
The text is a fiction excerpt, with a camera apparently recording the scene at the end.
